title: Horrified - A Perfect Game (for what it is)
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wBWXzI7uJYo

Daniel (@dungeondive) calls Horrified a perfect game for what it is: simple, quick to teach, gorgeous on the table, and the gold standard for gateway games. He has bought it around five times for family and friends. He credits Prospero Hall and Ravensburger, and marvels that a game of this quality sits in Target and Walmart when the Toys R Us aisles of his youth held two good games between them.

The reverence starts on the back of the board, which reprints a silent-movie-style warning ("you are about to unfold one of the strangest tales ever told... we warned you"). Heroes — archaeologist, mayor, courier, scientist — gather colour-coded items scattered across the village into sets against whichever Universal monsters are in play, each monster its own mini-game: cure the Wolf Man with blue science items, restore humanity to Frankenstein's monster and his bride, hunt down the Invisible Man, smash Dracula's coffins with weapons totalling six, row through the Black Lagoon. Difficulty is set simply by how many monsters you fight. The player aids are so considered that the Mummy's setup is printed on the back of every other monster's card, so you never flip.

His only knocks: the plastic monster minis are merely okay — he'd have preferred standees in the game's own art — and there is no expansion adding one more layer of complexity, which is why he never reaches for it solo. As the game to hand to newcomers, he cannot imagine better.

----

Horrified is Daniel's go-to gateway and most-gifted game. Which game have you bought most often for other people, and did it hook anyone?
